The uniform prior on k makes r non-uniform on [0.5, 2], with density concentrated near small r. This is a testable trade-off, because errors are measured in k-space. Comparing reciprocal, log and identity target transforms on the same backbone isolates whether the gain comes from this physical structure or just from any compressive transform.

Clipping predicted r to [0.5, 2] before reciprocation is valid because the true r lies in that box (k in [0.5, 2]).
The series-resistance intuition (steady-state and slow-mode physics) carries over at least partly to the transient window observed.
